headline: IAEA officials recently inspected Bushehr nuclear plant, Iran says
dek: Baghaei says Iran has not suspended its nuclear commitment, but US/Israeli attacks on its facilities have 'hindered the normal implementation of safeguards arrangements'. He says the IAEA board of governors and director general 'failed to fulfil their legal obligations' by overlooking the…
sources: Esmaeil Baghaei, Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman, weekly press conference, via Al Jazeera liveblog
fault_line: Can the IAEA still verify Iran's programme, or has inspection become a bargaining chip in the war?

sections.what_happened: Baghaei says Iran has not suspended its nuclear commitment, but US/Israeli attacks on its facilities have 'hindered the normal implementation of safeguards arrangements'. He says the IAEA board of governors and director general 'failed to fulfil their legal obligations' by overlooking the aggression against Iran's facilities, that professional communication between Iran's Vienna mission and the agency continues, and that 'the recent inspection of the Bushehr nuclear power plant serves as evidence that this regulated cooperation continues.'
sections.what_verified: 1 declared-tier family (Al Jazeera, T2) carrying the spokesman's own statement -- primary_source_single_family: true.
sections.what_disputed: The IAEA has not publicly confirmed a recent Bushehr inspection as of this scan; Baghaei's own framing concedes safeguards implementation is 'hindered' by the attacks, which cuts against full cooperation; the agency's last public reporting on Iran (June 13, 2025) put the 60%-enriched stockpile at 440.9 kg with access already restricted.
sections.why_matters: While the world argues about the 440.9 kg stockpile, inspectors were quietly back inside Bushehr -- what did they see, and why won't the IAEA say so?
sections.context: Background: IN-WINDOW -- IAEA officials recently inspected Bushehr nuclear plant, Iran says; Tehran insists its nuclear commitment is not suspended

totw_analysis: Our read: While the world argues about the 440.9 kg stockpile, inspectors were quietly back inside Bushehr -- what did they see, and why won't the IAEA say so? The fault line our audience is arguing over: Can the IAEA still verify Iran's programme, or has inspection become a bargaining chip in the war?
